options: A required field that changes how a resource actually behaves
A key-value metadata pair attached to a resource, used for organization and cost tracking
A snapshot of a resource's configuration at a point in time
A permission that controls who can access a resource
questions.explain: Tags are pure metadata, like Environment: Production — they don't change behavior, only organization and reporting.

questions.q: What does `aws ec2 create-tags --resources i-0abcd1234efgh5678 --tags Key=Environment,Value=Production` do?
options: Applies an Environment=Production tag to that existing EC2 instance
Only works if the instance is already stopped
Deletes any existing tags on that instance
Creates a brand-new EC2 instance named Production
questions.explain: create-tags applies one or more Key=Value pairs to one or more existing resource IDs.

questions.q: How can you tag an EC2 instance at the moment it's created, instead of tagging it afterward?
options: Pass --tag-specifications as part of the aws ec2 run-instances command
Use aws ec2 describe-instances with a --tags flag
It's not possible — all tagging must happen after create-tags
Tags can only ever be added through the console, never the CLI
questions.explain: --tag-specifications on run-instances applies tags in the same call that creates the instance, so nothing is briefly untagged.

questions.q: What does --filters "Name=tag:Environment,Value=Production" do when added to aws ec2 describe-instances?
options: Sorts instances alphabetically by tag name
Returns only the instances that carry that exact tag
Has no effect unless combined with --query
Deletes the Environment tag from every instance
questions.explain: --filters narrows which resources describe-instances returns in the first place, before --query reshapes the result.

questions.q: What has to happen before a user-defined tag like CostCenter shows up as its own line in Cost Explorer?
options: It must be activated as a Cost Allocation Tag in the AWS Billing console
It must be renamed with an aws: prefix
Nothing — every tag appears in Cost Explorer automatically the moment it's applied
It must be applied to every resource in the account, with no exceptions
questions.explain: User-defined tags need manual activation under Cost Allocation Tags, and it can take up to 24 hours to populate after that.
